data.body:
## ROOT CAUSE — PROVEN (transient runner-FS INDEX-write fault, self-heal coverage gap)

The production `rebar create` write surfaced `fatal: unable to write new index file` because
that signature is the ONE member of git's runner-FS transient WRITE family that the store's
shared self-heal does not cover.

### Mechanism (cited to git + the store seam)
- `stage_and_commit` (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`) runs `_git_add` then `_git_commit`
  (`src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py`). Both compose the shared retries
  `_with_index_lock_retry` (OUTER, index.lock contention + stale reclaim) around
  `_with_transient_fault_retry` (INNER, runner-FS transient faults).
- The INNER retry fires only on `git_outcome.TRANSIENT_WRITE_MARKERS`
  (`src/rebar/_store/git_outcome.py`): `unable to create temporary file`,
  `failed to insert into database`, `unable to index file`. All three are the object-DB
  loose-object temp-create member of the family.
- `fatal: unable to write new index file` is git's lockfile-commit failure for the INDEX
  write (`read-cache.c` `write_locked_index`/`do_write_index` via `commit_lock_file`),
  emitted by `git add` / `git write-tree` / a commit's pre-ref-update index prep. Confirmed
  present verbatim in this host's git binary string catalog (`/opt/homebrew/bin/git`).
- It matches NONE of the transient markers today (verified at runtime):
  `is_transient_object_write("...unable to write new index file")` -> False,
  `is_index_lock` -> False, `is_git_lock` -> False, `is_invalid_object` -> False. So it is
  returned on the FIRST attempt as a hard `StoreError` and surfaces to the caller — exactly
  the reported "operator retry required".
- The transient fingerprint matches the report: 458 GiB free, ample inodes, clean status
  afterward, no `index.lock`, and an identical retried create succeeded — a filesystem hiccup
  on the index write, not a data fault or lock contention.

### Idempotency / safety of the retry (AC: recovery commits exactly one intended event)
git has a SEPARATE, distinct message for a POST-ref-update index-write failure:
`repository has been updated, but unable to write` + `new_index file.` (underscore). That
string does NOT contain the contiguous substring `unable to write new index file`, so the
marker cannot match it (verified: `is_transient_object_write(post_ref_msg)` -> False).
Therefore a match provably means git had NOT yet moved HEAD — no commit landed — so re-running
`git add`/`git commit` cannot duplicate or omit an event. This is consistent with the
production evidence that an exact-title search found NO created ticket (the failed write left
nothing committed). Under the exclusive write lock the retry also cannot overwrite a concurrent
ticket write.

### Reconciliation with lowcost-unsainted-wallaby (50b1)
That ticket correctly kept this string OUT of the index-lock CONTENTION classifier
(`_is_git_lock_error`), because in its TEST the message came from the test's own timer deleting
git's real `index.lock` (force-reclaiming it would have masked a test bug). That reasoning is
about the lock/force-reclaim path and is unchanged here. This fix adds the string to the
runner-FS transient WRITE family instead — a bounded backoff RE-RUN with NO reclaim — which is
the mechanism the sibling object-DB faults already use. The two paths do not overlap.

### Origin (caused_by)
The transient-write marker table was introduced by edf7-946e-84be-48b3 ("retry transient git
object-DB failure on `git add`") covering only the object-DB temp-create signatures; the
sibling index-write signature was omitted from that family at creation, and stayed omitted when
the table was consolidated into `git_outcome` (unheedful-custodial-bluebottle) and extended to
`git commit` (interior-raspberry-titi). This bug is the residual of that coverage gap.
